heard: NASA fired an 820-pound copper bullet into a speeding comet. On July 4, 2005, the Deep Impact Mission intercepted Comet Tempel 1 with a two-part spacecraft. The mothership released a smart impactor for a collision at 23,000 miles per hour. Engineers used copper to ensure the strike wouldn't contaminate scientific readings of the comet's minerals. The collision released energy equal to 5 tons of TNT, ejecting a massive cloud of debris. Telescopes initially saw only a blur because the spacecraft's primary camera was out of focus. Scientists used complex math to sharpen the view, revealing a vault of organic ingredients for life. In 2011, a second mission confirmed the strike carved a crater 150 meters wide.
